questions.question: What happens when sugar dissolves in water, and how do we know the sugar is still there?
questions.expected_answer: The sugar breaks up into pieces far too small to see, and they spread evenly all through the water, so the sugar seems to disappear and the water looks clear. We know it is still there because the water tastes sweet.

questions.question: What is a solution? Give three ways to tell a solution from a mixture like sand and water.
questions.expected_answer: A solution is a uniform mixture, the same all the way through, made when a solid dissolves in a liquid. In a solution you cannot see the dissolved solid, it is clear though it may be coloured, nothing settles to the bottom, and a filter cannot separate it. In sand and water you can see the grains, the water is cloudy while stirred, the sand settles, and a filter catches it.

questions.question: Give three examples of solutions in everyday life.
questions.expected_answer: Sweet tea or rooibos, cooldrink, sea water, salt water, some medicines, the sugar and salt drink used for diarrhoea, soil water with dissolved minerals, and blood carrying dissolved sugar and salts.
